findings.claim: The new reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source within this compilation. Diagnostics created with a null or Location.None location (for example GetIdentifierLocation returning null for metadata types, or other paths with no location) used to be reported and are now silently suppressed. This is a behavior change for same-assembly types too. Previously reported location-less diagnostics, such as MsgPack003/004/005 errors, may no longer appear in users' builds, so invalid code could compile cleanly.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests for MsgPack003/004/005 and any diagnostic created with a null location (e.g. Diagnostic.Create with a null location from GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation on a type in the same compilation). Assert the diagnostic is still reported on head as on base. Fail if any diagnostic with Location.None that base reported is now missing.

findings.claim: Filtering all diagnostics by tree membership also hides diagnostics for source types in the same compilation if the location came from a different compilation's syntax tree, e.g. partial or generated trees. Diagnostics previously reported are now dropped, and it is unclear whether the MemberNeedsKey fix (FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()) is consistent with the wrapper for null-location members.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the TypeCollector paths that call reportDiagnostic with null or Location.None locations, and compare with base behavior. Confirm via the existing analyzer test suite that no expected diagnostic goes missing.
